notes: Both coders found the same two university-level documents (Provost faculty guidance with two Faculty Council syllabus templates; Learning Design AI guidance) and no school or computing policy. Matched units mostly agreed on actor and modality. Disagreements: (1) phase for the same passage (course-start vs before-course for syllabus statements, general vs during-work for privacy and ethics principles), resolved by whether the passage is an expectation sent to students, a general principle, or advice about using a tool; (2) policy_type for four passages (detailed citation P24 vs P25, student content generation P91 vs P15, feedback P101 vs P59 on one sentence the coders split, and student-work data entry P50 vs P20), resolved against the type definitions and the source sentence; (3) unit_stance for misconduct-classification and licence-fact sentences (restrict or encourage vs neutral), resolved as neutral because they classify or state facts. Eleven units were found by one coder only: eight kept (A, 5: ethical-use violations sentence, resource location, research-topic prompting, student accuracy check, GPTZero mention; B, 3: generic cite-sources sentence, student Q&A tutoring, authentic-assessment recommendation) and three dropped (A: restatement of the two-statement sentence as P05, and a Faculty Council minutes citation that is provenance and not a policy; B: the evaluate-student-work half of one feedback sentence, merged into the P101 unit; this makes four B-only units with three kept and one merged, and seven A-only with five kept and two dropped). Where B had a normalized policy and A had an anchor that omitted AI or the tool name, the B wording was used. No new types proposed.
